answer: Each beacon plants a pigment-banded flag in tundra permafrost and photos it beside an onyx reference stone; the flag's dye fades at a fixed UV rate, so the color ratio proves the flag stood there today, not last week. Flag GPS, fade ratio and beacon ID hash into the next block. A reading counts only if the fade sits inside the season's daylight band and the probe shows the ground still frozen solid. Faking 1,000 flags costs $140,000 in pigment kits and $60,000 in Arctic charters, plus 100 POA bonded per beacon, slashed on mismatch — like forging footprints in snow that never fell.
